title: (replay, the wall clock decides step counts): the stage's load after the star is chosen runs in slices of 4 ms of wall time (GameScene::initAfterScenarioChosen, GameScene.cpp:165-217; the placement's own deadline, StageDataHolder.cpp:168 and PlacementInfoOrdered.cpp:139), resumed once a frame from the star select's nerves (ScenarioSelectScene.cpp:277, :312, :320, through GameSystemSceneController.cpp:151-163), and each of those frames runs the scene's update and the star select's (GameSystemSceneController.cpp:240-251, :480-487). A skipped cutscene runs extra steps in a frame while 9 ms of wall time last (NebulaCutsceneSkip.cpp:46-47, tryExtraStep :384-399, GameSystem.cpp:199-202). So how many frames lie between the choice and play, and how many steps a skip runs in each frame, follow the computer's speed; the game's random stream is seeded before the star select (GameSystemSceneController.cpp:127), so a draw in those frames would move it by machine. The placement's id sets are found by a scan of every set per placement (PlacementInfoOrdered.cpp:157-166), quadratic in a level's placements.
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Demo and Game/Scene reports (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the stage loads on a load worker (or in one piece) and no frame steps game state that the stage keeps while it loads; a skip runs a fixed number of steps per frame or runs to its end with the input held; the id sets found through a map. To show with the probe (P-242): the step hash at play's first step on a fast and a slowed machine. Replay: identical once the load and the skip no longer read the clock.
